title: Instruction List: calling an off-delay and an on-delay timer
summary: Call a TOF timer with CAL to keep a light on after a button is released, and a TON timer to ignore a sensor blip that is too short, then read each timer output with LD.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence with one 10 ms task; they do not establish electrical debounce, sensor response or target timing, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Call a timer instance with CAL, passing its input and its preset, and read its output with LD.
Keep an output on for a fixed time after its input drops, using TOF, and ignore an input that is on for less than a fixed time, using TON.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/Delays.il the timers HoldTimer (TOF) and FilterTimer (TON) are declared but not called. A timer is not a single instruction: CAL HoldTimer(IN := Button, PT := T#300ms) runs it with its inputs, and a following LD HoldTimer.Q loads its output into the current result, ready for ST. Light must stay ON for {{t:300}} ms after Button is released. Confirmed must turn ON only after Sensor has stayed ON for {{t:200}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which timer keeps an output on and which one waits before turning it on.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: The scenario presses Button at {{t:100}} ms and releases it at {{t:300}} ms. Sensor blips ON from {{t:100}} ms to {{t:140}} ms and is ON again from {{t:500}} ms to {{t:900}} ms. Predict Light and Confirmed at {{t:200}}, {{t:450}}, {{t:650}} and {{t:800}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:Delays.Light=true,Delays.Confirmed=false@200|Light ON, Confirmed OFF}} at {{t:200}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=true,Delays.Confirmed=false@450|Light ON, Confirmed OFF}} at {{t:450}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=false,Delays.Confirmed=false@650|both OFF}} at {{t:650}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=false,Delays.Confirmed=true@800|Confirmed ON, Light OFF}} at {{t:800}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter flaw, save it, then press Check: The starting program loads each input and stores it in the output, so Light is already OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed turns ON for the {{t:100}} ms blip; call HoldTimer with Button as IN and T#300ms as PT, then load HoldTimer.Q and store it in Light, and do the same with FilterTimer, Sensor and T#200ms for Confirmed.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named Delays and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Follow Light and Confirmed in the trace: the short blip never turns Confirmed ON, Light is still ON at {{t:450}} ms although Button went OFF at {{t:300}} ms, and Confirmed rises about {{t:200}} ms after Sensor came back at {{t:500}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: Light falls about {{t:300}} ms after Button, and Confirmed rises about {{t:200}} ms after the second Sensor pulse.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Swap the two timers in your head: what would a TON on Button and a TOF on Sensor do with this scenario?
stages.checkpoint: TON delays the start and TOF delays the end; each answers a different question about a signal. In IL both are called the same way, so the declaration decides which one you get.

hints.text: TOF keeps its Q on for the preset time after IN falls, and TON raises Q only after IN has been on for the preset time. CAL runs the timer; LD Timer.Q reads its output.
CAL HoldTimer(IN := Button, PT := T#300ms), LD HoldTimer.Q, ST Light; CAL FilterTimer(IN := Sensor, PT := T#200ms), LD FilterTimer.Q, ST Confirmed.

faultCases: The starting program loads each input and stores it in the output, so Light is already OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed turns ON for the {{t:100}} ms blip; call HoldTimer with Button as IN and T#300ms as PT, then load HoldTimer.Q and store it in Light, and do the same with FilterTimer, Sensor and T#200ms for Confirmed.
